13:00 Local Time, 07:30 GMT, 13:00 IST: The series has already produced more than enough batting fireworks and the third ODI arrives with India 2-0 up. Virat Kohli’s 139 in the first game, Rohit Sharma’s 101 in the second and Shubman Gill’s unbeaten 223 in Guwahati have proven just how dominant India’s batting has been. Gill’s double-century, completed in only 117 balls, was the centrepiece of a record chase as India hunted down 406 with eight wickets and 39 balls to spare.

West Indies, though, have hardly been short of runs. Their 405 for 7 in Guwahati was their highest total in men’s ODIs, with John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo all scoring hundreds in the same innings. It was a remarkable batting effort from West Indies, with three of their batters reaching centuries, but even a total of 405 for 7 could not prevent India from completing another emphatic run chase.

Now the series moves to New Chandigarh, where the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium will host its first men’s ODI. With the result of the series already decided, India have the luxury of looking at the bigger picture, while West Indies have one last chance to put together the kind of all-round performance that has so far eluded them. After two games dominated by the bat, the question is whether the final ODI can offer something different.

Keemo Paul (1/2): [What was the chat there with Shai struggling a bit?] Well yeah, obviously when I was in the middle with Shai, the plan was just to try and keep the required runs under eight runs per over. So that was basically the plan, like you said, Shai was struggling a bit. So I knew I had to take a few chances. [What was the discussions in the dressing room knowing that Jewell was injured?] Well yeah, I mean coach spoke to us saying we were just trying to break the game down in phases. I mean we saw India batted in the last two games and chasing is always good on these wickets. So we always had the confidence. We backed ourselves and we got the job done tonight. So that's awesome.

Paul (2/2): [Appreciation for your captain?] Definitely, definitely. Shai, he's a modern-day legend, man. And the way he's batted this series is quite amazing. So yeah, definitely. [On his performance going forward] Well, for me it's just now to get complacent. I just want to take it as a stepping stone and contribute to the team whenever I get the opportunity. I just want to keep performing. I'm happy and yeah, just do my best always. [Your thoughts on your bowling?] Well, like it's from the past two games, we had our plans. We were just trying to hit that length as hard as possible, the top of the stump length. So that was basically the plan on these wickets. It's quite tough. So you got to bring your skills out, try to scramble, seam the ball as much as possible. So that was my plan.

Hope (2/2): [On West Indies' record run chase and the overall ODI series] I think we played some really good cricket in patches. The batters were scoring some runs. That's what we really wanted to do. So yeah, we've been doing really well for the last two, three years where batters have been more consistent. We asked them to put big scores on the board. It's always difficult bowling in these conditions. We know India, more batter friendly. You got to bring your skills out and very, very, very small margins for error. So from a bowling standpoint, we learned a lot. I'm sure the guys are going to take this and hopefully we can get a lot better in the bowling side of things going forward. [On recovering in time for the upcoming shorter format] So hopefully, I got two days to turn things around, so hopefully I'm match ready.

Gill collects the trophy and joins his team-mates. They pose with the WINNERS board. India won the first two matches convincingly with their top three batters doing the bulk of the scoring. Today, they lost Gill and Kohli cheaply. Rohit stepped up and missed out on another ton by 8 runs, Ruturaj Gaikwad scored 57 after being dropped four times but it was KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 that powered India to 351. In reply, captain Shai Hope opened the innings today and batted till the end to take his team over the winning line with a magnificent 162*, stitching four 50+ stands. Three matches were played in different parts of the country but the pattern remained similar. Good batting wickets, high-scoring encounters, centurions for both teams and the chasing team emerging victorious. It's time to bring the curtains down on this ODI series. The action now shifts to the shortest format. The 5-match T20I series commences on Tuesday (October 6th) and we'll be bringing you all the action. Until then, goodbye...
